subject: Coordination: safe-delete cadence, backup carve-out & subprocessor notice

From: John Kelly <john.k@acmehealth.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com
Cc: privacy@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data retention carve-out & backup purge timing

Connor —

Thanks for taking this on. We're starting our DPA amendment review and need clarity on two things before we can route to legal: 1) your deletion workflow for user-initiated erasure (what's removed immediately vs what remains in backups), and 2) backup purge timeline and whether Redwood can support a temporary carve-out for a 180-day investigation hold if required by regulators.

A few specific asks:
- Can you supply a short runbook that shows the sequence of actions from request to complete erasure (including KV cache, search indexes, and DB snapshots)?
- Do you have an approved subprocessors list and SOC2 evidence we can attach to our vendor review?
- If Redwood requires a shorter backup purge window by default, is there an exception process and SLA for granting temporary holds?

We're trying to line this up with our procurement timeline (targeting signature by July 9). Appreciate a pragmatic proposal.

—John
Head of Privacy, Acme Health
(attachment: initial-dpa-asks.pdf)

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com, jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com, laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data retention carve-out & backup purge timing

John — thanks for the clear asks. Short answer: we can meet the auditability needs without blocking production, but it requires an explicit carve-out in the DPA and an ops-runbook we agree on. High-level proposal below; I'll attach a concise runbook after legal input.

Proposed approach (draft):
- Immediate delete: remove primary indexes, user-facing records, and mark customer blobs for deletion within 24–72 hours after request.
- Backup retention default: snapshots are scheduled for purge at 90 days post-snapshot.
- Exception flow: temporary holds of up to 180 days can be granted with an authorized request from Acme Legal and Redwood CS/Compliance signoff; during hold the snapshot is pinned to an encrypted escrow storage and inaccessible to product traffic.
- Canary deletion: we run a canary purge in a non-prod partition to validate purge scripts before production snapshot deletion.

Attachments I plan to send: DPA_Amendment_v2.docx (legal redline), Subprocessor_Matrix.csv, Retention_Runbook_Summary.pdf (ops).

If that high level sounds acceptable, Kimberly/legal can turn the DPA language into a clean signature-ready doc and we can route to DocuSign. I'll loop in Security for SOC2 evidence.

Next step: Kimberly — can you take a look at the carve-out language and propose suggested redlines?

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
(attached: DPA_Amendment_v2.docx)

Subject: Re: Data retention carve-out & backup purge timing (redlines)

Connor/All —

I've reviewed the draft proposal and marked several legal items to include in the amendment. High-level redlines:
1) Define "temporary hold" mechanics: who can request, required supporting documentation, and an automatic review cadence (30/60/90 days) with expiration unless extended.
2) Escrow storage: specify encryption-at-rest, access controls, and export controls for cross-border holds.
3) Audit rights: Acme gets the right to verify retention actions once per year during normal operations and ad-hoc during a regulatory investigation (with mutual NDAs).
4) Subprocessors: we'll append the current Subprocessor_Matrix.csv to the DPA and include a 30-day notice period for new subprocessors (or immediate notice if newly added for Acme's account).

Operational asks from legal: provide a concise runbook (non-sensitive) for the emergency hold flow, and include SOC2 control copies (security can redact specific IP addresses).

I'll prepare a clean DPA with these redlines and circulate for internal sign-off; once we have Acme's reply we can push to DocuSign.

—Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
(attached: legal-redlines-summary.pdf)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Data retention carve-out & backup purge timing (technical constraints)

Team —

A few technical clarifications that should be represented in the runbook and DPA:
- System boundaries: snapshots are multi-tiered. We have short-lived incremental logs (retained 14–30 days) and full daily snapshots (retained per policy). Pinning a full snapshot to escrow increases storage I/O/space and requires a manual retention marker.
- Logs: we cannot selectively retain only certain search indexes without retaining the underlying shard snapshots for the period. If Acme wants index-level hold, we have to accept the storage cost or implement an export-to-escrow workflow (recommended).
- Forensic access: during a hold, access is limited to named personnel and readonly keys; any forensic restore must be scheduled and audited.

Operational impact estimate (very rough):
- Single 180-day hold on a standard account: +12–18% storage OPEX for the hold duration depending on snapshot frequency.
- Escrow migration (if required): 48–96 hours operational lead time and change window.

I'll draft the technical annex for the runbook and include exact subsystem names/IDs for legal to reference.

—Jonas
Director, Compliance & Controls
